airport.name: Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto International Airport

summary: Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto International Airport (NBJ) is Angola's newest and largest aviation hub, located in Ícolo e Bengo approximately 40 km southeast of Luanda. Named after Angola's first president, the airport was officially inaugurated in November 2023 to replace the older Quatro de Fevereiro Airport as the country's primary international gateway. The modern facility features a single large terminal capable of handling millions of passengers annually, along with a long runway suitable for wide-body intercontinental flights.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Luanda city center?
A: The airport is located about 40 km (25 miles) southeast of central Luanda, in the municipality of Ícolo e Bengo.

Q: When did Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto International Airport open?
A: The airport was inaugurated in late 2023 and began commercial operations, gradually replacing Luanda's older Quatro de Fevereiro Airport as the main international gateway.

Q: Does the airport have facilities for long-haul international flights?
A: Yes, it features a 4,000-meter runway capable of accommodating the largest commercial aircraft, including wide-body jets used for intercontinental routes.

Q: Who is the airport named after?
A: It is named after Dr. António Agostinho Neto, Angola's first president and a key figure in the country's independence movement from Portugal in 1975.
local_tip: Keep your passport and boarding pass easily accessible during the drive in—security checkpoints along the route to the airport are common, and having documents ready can speed up the journey significantly.
